ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, and senior managers must undergo comprehensive screening against the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Taiwan's own sanctions list maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Additionally, screening against international PEP databases (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones) is mandatory. Enhanced due diligence is required for any individual identified as a PEP, including verification of source of funds and source of wealth. Screening must be conducted at onboarding and on a continuous basis using automated monitoring tools. Any positive hit triggers immediate escalation to the AML Compliance Officer and may necessitate filing a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) of Taiwan. The protocol also includes adverse media checks and cross-referencing with corporate registry data to ensure no shell or nominee structures are used.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Traditional Chinese characters. An English name may be registered as a secondary name. The name must consist of a distinctive trade name, a business type, and a legal form designation (e.g., 'Limited'). Transliteration of foreign names must follow the official Mandarin romanization system (Hanyu Pinyin). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. Four-tier naming convention: (1) trade name, (2) business type, (3) region or locality, (4) additional designations such as 'International' or 'Holding'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written statement of reasons, evidence of distinctiveness, and any prior use of the name. The MOEA will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 60 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review at the Taipei High Court. The appeal process does not extend the name reservation period; a new reservation must be filed if the original reservation expires. The applicant should also consider alternative names to avoid delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible for registration purposes under Taiwan's Company Act, provided a physical address is designated for service of process. However, for the digital advertising and media buying industry, banks and tax authorities may reject virtual offices due to heightened AML/CFT risks. The Ministry of Finance requires a physical presence for VAT registration and may conduct on-site inspections. The Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) expects financial institutions to verify the physical existence of the business. Therefore, a virtual office is not recommended; a physical office with a dedicated mailbox and staff is advisable to ensure compliance and smooth banking operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Registered office must have a visible sign and be accessible during business hours; (2) Business records must be maintained at the registered office; (3) VAT invoices must be issued from the registered address; (4) Employees must be present during inspections. Risk of unannounced physical inspection is moderate (estimated 30% annually) for companies in the advertising sector, especially those with cross-border transactions. Inspections are conducted by the National Taxation Bureau and the Company Registry. Triggers include inconsistent filings, high-value cash transactions, or third-party complaints.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Chapters I through III, including Articles 1, 2, 6, 8, 18, 29, 31, 100, 131, 156, 172, 173, 174, 193, 202, 207, 208, 218, 387 and 388; Company Registration and Operation Rules; Foreign Investment Act Articles 4, 5 and 7.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services, Company Registration Division, and the authorized special municipal or county/city company registration offices.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration accompanied by approved Articles of Incorporation and a bank capital verification certificate, filed under the Company Registration and Operation Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a general digital advertising and joint venture company under the Taiwan Companies Act. However, the registered capital must be fully subscribed in the Articles of Incorporation, and each shareholder's contribution must be deposited into a segregated corporate capital account at a licensed bank in Taiwan and verified by the bank before registration. No governmental blocked escrow account is required. The capital may be used as working capital after registration, but it may not be returned to shareholders before a lawful distribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF SINO-FOREIGN EQUITY JOINT VENTURE LTD.

A meeting of the Board of Directors of the Company was duly convened and held at the registered office on the date set forth below. Notice having been waived by all directors, the meeting constituted a valid quorum under the Companies Act of Taiwan and the Articles of Incorporation. The Chairperson noted receipt of the certificate of incorporation from the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services, and referred to the following matters requiring formal approval.

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL. The Board reviewed the statement of capital subscription and the bank capital verification certificate, and resolved that the registered share capital of the Company, amounting to the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation, is subscribed and allotted to the founding shareholders in the proportions set forth in the subscription schedule. All subscriptions shall be fully paid before any distribution of assets or issuance of share certificates. The capital verification certificate issued by a licensed bank shall be deposited in the corporate records.

2. AUTHORIZATION OF BANKING ARRANGEMENTS. The Board resolved to approve the opening of one or more corporate bank accounts with licensed banks in Taiwan. The Chairperson, General Manager, and Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly in any two-signature combination, are hereby authorized to execute account opening forms, signatory cards, electronic banking authorizations, wire transfer instructions, and foreign exchange documents. Each bank is empowered to rely on this resolution until it receives a written revocation.

3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopted the registered office located at the principal place of business in Taiwan as the statutory office and official address for service of notices, tax communications, and legal process.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board unanimously appointed and approved the Chairperson, General Manager, Company Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer named in the minutes. Each officer accepted the appointment and acknowledged the fiduciary duties imposed by law. The officers are authorized to execute contracts, open bank accounts, appoint legal counsel, and conduct the ordinary business affairs of the Company.

RESOLVED FURTHER that the Chairperson and Company Secretary are authorized to execute all government filing forms, declarations, tax registrations, and permit applications, and to pay all statutory fees required to commence operations. All acts done by the incorporators prior to this meeting for the purpose of forming the Company are ratified, confirmed, and adopted as acts of the Company. This resolution may be certified by the Company Secretary and shall remain in full force until amended or revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board. ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY this date set forth in the board minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services Company Name Checking System; Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission for foreign and joint venture investment approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online pre-screening of proposed English and Chinese company names on the MOEA company name checking system, then submit a formal Application for Company Name Reservation together with the draft Articles of Incorporation and the proposed business scope. For a Sino-foreign equity joint venture, submit a parallel Foreign Investment Application to the MOEA Investment Commission under the Foreign Investment Act, attaching the shareholder table, source-of-funds statement, registered capital amount, and the exact ISIC 7310 description showing pure digital advertising services. The competent officer will examine name distinctiveness, nationality restrictions, and conformity with Taiwan business registration policy. No substantive business may be launched before the name reservation certificate and investment approval are issued. The applicant should monitor the electronic case status and use the designated amendments channel to revise any deficient fields.
required_dossiers: Application for Company Name Reservation
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents or passport copies of all directors and shareholders
JV foreign investment application with shareholding structure
Power of attorney if filed through an agent
Business plan or feasibility statement for the foreign investment review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on similarity grounds or the foreign investment application is queried, the applicant has 30 days to file a written explanation or amended filing. A supplementary name list of up to three alternatives may be submitted. If the MOEA Investment Commission issues a suspension notice, the company must substantiate the lawful source of capital and the non-sensitive nature of digital advertising operations. An administrative appeal may be lodged within 30 days after formal denial.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Capital Deposit and Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Taiwan designated by the founders; the bank's branch office handles the capital verification certificate and foundation account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the name reservation and investment approval are received, the founders must open a temporary or foundation bank account in the exact reserved company name. Each shareholder must remit the subscribed capital directly from its own banking account, and the remittance records must identify the payor and stated purpose. Once the funds are received, the bank will issue a Capital Verification Certificate confirming the amount held and the account title. If any shareholder contributes equipment or intangible assets rather than cash, an independent Taiwanese appraiser must issue a valuation report and the asset must be fully transferred. The Company is prohibited from withdrawing or returning the capital prior to company registration. The verified capital after registration becomes the working capital of the Company and is not held under a governmental blocked escrow scheme.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation certificate
Foreign investment approval letter if applicable
Draft Articles of Incorporation indicating capital and shareholders
Passports or national IDs of all directors and shareholders
Beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declaration form
Bank capital verification certificate issued after deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the beneficial owner or source of funds, supply the corporate structure chart, apostilled identification documents, and bank reference letters. If remittance purpose codes are inconsistent with ISIC 7310, correct the wire instructions and obtain a revised remittance receipt. Any deficiency in the capital verification certificate should be cured before the registration filing; a revised certificate may be issued upon additional deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Registration to the MOEA Department of Commercial Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services, Company Registration Section or the authorized special municipal or county/city Company Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation registration package through the MOEA Company Registration One-Stop Service. The registrar will verify the Articles of Incorporation, the capital verification certificate, the registered office proof, and the directors' consents. Upon approval, the Company will be issued a Company Registration Certificate and gains juridical personality. The company seal may be engraved only after registration. The applicant must ensure that the English name, Chinese name, business scope, and officer data in the filing exactly match the foreign investment approval and the bank capital verification certificate. Any mismatch will cause a deficiency notice and delay issuance of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for Company Registration
Approved Articles of Incorporation
Company Name Reservation Certificate
Capital Verification Certificate from the bank
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Proof of registered office including lease, ownership certificate or landlord consent
Consents and identification of directors and statutory officers
Power of attorney if an agent signs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registry will issue the applicant a correction notice with a statutory cure period, generally 15 days and in some cases extended by 30 days. The applicant may supplement the affected dossiers online or at the service counter. If the registration is rejected, the applicant can resubmit a fresh application or appeal to the MOEA under administrative appeal rules; the filing fee may be preserved for the resubmission within the prescribed window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Labor Insurance, and National Health Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Administration, District Taxation Office; Ministry of Labor, Bureau of Labor Insurance; National Health Insurance Administration regional office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of receiving the Company Registration Certificate, the responsible person must apply for tax registration and obtain a business registration certificate and uniform invoice number. The company must also register as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration even if the first employee is being hired at the same time. Withholding tax on employees and foreign vendors will be applied, and the company should file monthly business tax returns even during zero-revenue periods. Digital advertising vendors should also apply for an electronic invoice certificate and issue electronic invoices for all domestic media arbitrage transactions. Any paid-in capital or foreign exchange proceeds must be reported through the Central Bank foreign exchange declaration process.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Company seal
Articles of Incorporation
Responsible person's identification and specimen signature
Registered office lease or property use certificate
Bank account details and capital verification certificate
Application for tax registration and uniform invoice
Labor insurance and national health insurance employer registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority requires supplemental information, use the online application system to send revised attachments within 14 days. If the labor insurance registration is returned for missing employee data, register the employment after the employee's identity is received and provide backdated compensation to avoid coverage gaps. Penalties for late tax registration may be abated through a written explanation to the tax authority on reasonable-cause grounds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Startup, Bank Signatory Mandates and Premises Safety Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's statutory officers, external corporate counsel and certified public accountants, and the local fire and workplace safety management office for ordinary office occupancy.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Organize the first statutory board meeting and adopt the formal board resolution included in this dossier. The certified resolution will be used to complete corporate bank mandates, appoint the responsible person, and issue share certificates to shareholders. For ISIC 7310 digital advertising, affiliate media buying, and lead generation, no special industrial operating license is required; however, all contracts with advertisers and publishers should be executed under the company name after legal formality. The operations team should prepare an AML and KYC program for enhanced-risk clients because the banking AML risk tier is medium risk. The registered office must maintain fire extinguishers, smoke detectors, and emergency exits consistent with the Fire Services Act and Occupational Safety and Health Act, and must obtain a fire safety management plan if the building's occupancy permit requires it.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of First Board Resolution
Director identification and sample signatures
Bank account opening forms and signatory cards
Share certificates or register of shareholders
AML and KYC risk assessment policy documents
Office lease, workplace inspection record, and fire safety equipment checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank declines to open accounts due to perceived money-laundering risk in media buying, present the licensed business scope, source-of-funds files, and board resolution, or approach an alternate bank recommended by the investment commission. Any deficiency in structural fire safety must be corrected by installing required equipment and resubmitting the inspection certificate before the office can be continuously occupied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, physical assembly, or warehousing activities are conducted under ISIC 7310, which is digital advertising media arbitrage and affiliate lead generation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory industrial operating license is required for affiliate media buying in Taiwan; general company registration and tax registration are sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Taiwan Ministry of Environment and Environmental Protection Administration have no EIA mandate for this non-industrial digital service activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no Environmental Impact Assessment report, self-verification document, or environmental registration certificate is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company will not generate wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams associated with ISIC 7310. Ordinary office waste and limited e-waste disposal must be handled through licensed waste carriers under the Waste Disposal Act should any computer hardware be decommissioned.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at the industrial plant level. For the ordinary registered office, the company must maintain compliance with the Fire Services Act, including fire extinguishers, escape routes, and a fire safety management plan if required by the building occupancy permit, and must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act on workplace safety; no civil defense license is otherwise mandated.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taiwan – National Taxation Administration, acting through local National Tax Bureaus; online electronic portals: Taxation E-Platform (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw) and E-Invoice Integration Service Platform (https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Because the investing party is a mainland Chinese entity, the first mandatory step is to obtain inbound investment permission from the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, under the Regulations Governing the Permission of Investment in Taiwan from the Mainland Area. After approval, the Taiwan-incorporated joint venture must complete company registration under the Taiwan Company Act through the Ministry of Economic Affairs one-stop company registration system, which assigns the eight-digit Unified Business Number used as the tax identification number (TIN). Before commencing business, the company must file the Business Tax Registration Application with the competent local National Tax Bureau, attaching the company registration certificate, investment approval document, lease or place-of-business proof, and authorized representative identification. The National Tax Bureau then confirms the entity as a VAT-registered profit-seeking enterprise and issues the business tax registration certificate. Foreign non-resident shareholders are not issued separate Taiwan TINs for the local entity; payments of Taiwan-source income to such shareholders are subject to withholding by the Taiwan entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide a check-the-box entity classification election or a general OECD hybrid mismatch election. A Taiwan-incorporated limited liability company is mandatorily taxed at entity level under the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Taiwan Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Business tax registration is generally required before commencing business; the statutory exemption threshold below which a small business may remain unregistered is average monthly sales of NT$80,000 or less for goods and NT$40,000 or less for services. Once monthly sales exceed these thresholds, mandatory business tax registration is triggered. Additionally, a business with monthly sales below NT$200,000 may be treated as a small-scale business operator assessed at the 1% business tax rate instead of the standard 5% VAT, while monthly sales at or above NT$200,000 generally require mandatory Uniform Invoice issuance and full VAT accounting.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan requires VAT-registered businesses to issue Uniform Invoices for all taxable sales. Electronic Uniform Invoices must be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integration Service Platform through the Turnkey application programming interface or the e-service portal, where invoice data is archived and assigned a validation number. This is a post-issuance secure transmission mandate rather than a real-time fiscal pre-clearance stamping system. Mandatory cloud-based e-invoices apply to designated e-commerce, retail-chain, and high-volume digital-commerce sectors, and consumer-facing e-invoices must carry QR-code digital validation. Failure to transmit e-invoice data may result in Uniform Invoice penalties and suspension of tax benefits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 7 of the Taiwan Business Tax Act applies to goods physically exported from Taiwan under customs control and to services rendered in Taiwan that are actually used outside Taiwan, including cross-border digital advertising, affiliate media-buying, and lead-generation services performed for overseas clients. To claim 0% VAT, the taxpayer must hold a genuine and complete export or offshore-service file proving shipment or overseas use, and the foreign exchange proceeds must be collected through authorized banking channels.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Foreign Exchange Transaction Declaration and bank inward remittance settlement certificate or equivalent bank foreign exchange receipt evidence
Export Service Contract and proof of overseas utilization for offshore services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Administration may retrospectively reassess unsubstantiated or fraudulent zero-export claims as domestic taxable sales at the 5% VAT rate. Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, the taxpayer is liable for the underpaid tax plus a fine of not less than one time and not more than five times the additional tax amount. If the claim is supported by forged customs declarations, fictitious foreign exchange repatriation, or false service contracts, criminal liability may arise under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act, with imprisonment for up to five years, and the applicable tax assessment period is extended to seven years for tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) in coordination with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), with cross-strait RMB clearing routed through the Bank of China Taipei branch and supervised on the Taiwan side by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) and the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a bifurcated convertibility regime. Current-account items, including services-trade inflows and outflows for online advertising and affiliate media buying, settlement of dividends, and payment of platform fees, are fully convertible and may be settled directly at a domestic bank under SAFE post-verification without prior approval. Capital-account items, including FDI capital injection, equity transfers between the Taiwan investor and the joint venture, external borrowing, and repatriation of liquidation proceeds, require prior SAFE registration or approval. TWD is not freely convertible inside mainland China; receipts from Taiwan are normally settled in USD or CNH. Dividend remittance to the Taiwan corporate investor is permitted only after audited financial statements are filed, corporate income tax is settled, withholding at 10% is paid, and the FIE annual report is submitted. Cross-border online advertising service fees are treated as services trade and are outside the capital-account quota, but each remittance must carry a bona fide underlying contract and platform delivery evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory surrender of foreign exchange was abolished in 2012; the present rule is mandated repatriation with retained use. The joint venture must repatriate all export or services-trade proceeds, including affiliate commissions and advertising arbitrage revenue for overseas platforms, into its domestic settlement account under SAFE's Trade in Goods and Trade in Services Foreign Exchange Administration Measures. The statutory expectation is that proceeds enter China within the verification window of the relevant customs declaration or service invoice, and in practice no later than 180 days from the issuance of the underlying invoice; amounts outstanding beyond 90 days are flagged in the SAFE Total Amount Monitoring System and beyond 180 days trigger an explicit written explanation, bank lodging, and potential administrative penalty. Conversion of retained foreign currency into RMB is at the enterprise's commercial discretion, with no forced conversion ratio, and requires a bank-declared purpose with supporting documents.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for the China-domiciled joint venture. Offshore digital EMIs such as Mercury, Wise, and Currencycloud cannot onboard a China-incorporated entity because they hold no Chinese banking licence and SAFE prohibits a resident enterprise from maintaining undisclosed offshore bank balances. Wise Business does not support China-incorporated companies for USD or TWD receiving accounts. The practical alternative is a Taiwan or Hong Kong affiliate vehicle collecting platform payouts and executing EMI-based disbursements, while the China entity receives its earned margin via a licensed onshore settlement channel. Within China, licensed cross-border payment institutions registered with SAFE, such as LianLian, PingPong, and Payoneer through its licensed China partner, are the permissible fintech-style rails for affiliate revenue settlement; a direct foreign EMI account for the China entity is structurally disfavoured and treated as a round-tripping violation if it is used to hide onshore receipt obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is mandatory. Under PBOC account-opening confirmation rules and prevailing SAFE bank practice, the legal representative must appear in person at the bank counter for the initial interview, and the bank must conduct a two-person door-site verification at the registered business address. Where the risk score is elevated, the financial controller and the 25% or greater beneficial owner from Taiwan must also appear or provide a power of attorney authenticated by cross-strait notarisation and certified by the relevant local bureau. Remote or fully digital opening is not available for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture in the Medium-Risk Enhanced AML category.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ad-tech arbitrage opacity: unidentifiable traffic-sourced revenues and cascading payments to unknown publishers and media owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Google, Meta, and TikTok publisher or affiliate network master agreements; platform settlement and payout reports; granular campaign-level transaction log; publisher KYC file containing beneficial owner names and tax IDs; media invoice register; ISIC and NAICS scope certificate; three-month inbound and outbound cash-flow forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from the Taiwan investor with unclear source-of-funds provenance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Invested Enterprise establishment approval and business licence; SAFE FDI registration notice; investor constitutional documents; certified registry extracts; audited investor financials; source-of-wealth letter; remitting Taiwan bank statement chain showing the wire; proof of original funds via tax filings and prior bank statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity and low-ticket payout patterns that resemble structuring or smurfing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Affiliate payout policy and payment schedule; the bank-approved mass-payout whitelist arrangement; contractual media rate cards; advertising-platform reconciliation dashboard; tax invoice and withholding framework for Taiwan-resident affiliates; monthly treasury oversight report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and adverse-media overlap of Taiwan counterparties with restricted lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Daily automated sanctions screening log covering UN, EU, UK, OFAC, and PBOC lists; counterparty no-breach warranty letter; adverse-media investigation file; compliance certification signed by the joint venture's compliance officer; all cross-strait counterparty identity documents retained.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan or Hong Kong investor remits USD via SWIFT MT103, or CNH via CIPS, to the joint venture's FDI Capital Account at the Chinese custodian bank. The remittance is identified as direct investment by a foreign investor in the equity of a foreign-invested enterprise, referencing the SAFE FDI registration notice and the FIE business licence. The bank validates the instruction against the Capital Project Information System, books the funds, and converts them to RMB for permitted working-capital purposes such as rent, payroll, and advertising inventory procurement. No minimum statutory paid-in capital applies under the Foreign Investment Law 2020; the contribution schedule agreed in the joint venture contract governs. The capital injection itself is not subject to income tax, but a 10% withholding tax applies on any later dividend distribution to the Taiwan investor. Current-account receivables from Taiwan affiliates are routed to the USD settlement account under the SAFE services-trade purpose code for advertising, supported by the relevant contract and invoice retained for five years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Payments to overseas advertising platforms such as Google, Meta, TikTok, and X, and to Taiwan media vendors, are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for USD or TWD-converted-USD, and via CIPS for CNH-denominated payments to Taiwan counterparties using Bank of China Taipei as the RMB clearing counterparty. Every payment must be declared under the SAFE services-trade purpose code for advertising and market-research services, with the platform invoice, media-delivery proof such as impression logs, and the corresponding service agreement lodged at the bank. Same-day TWD disbursement to Taiwan publishers is not directly available onshore; treasury batches TWD through a USD side-rail with FX conversion at the Taiwan intermediary. The paying bank requires evidence of the withholding tax paid on VAT and enterprise income tax for cross-border services before the remittance is released. Letters of credit are not standard in performance-based media buying; the dominant rails are MT103 wires for vendor settlements and contract-referenced platform remittances.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD FX forward contracts and FX swaps with real services-trade or capital-injection exposure, entered under a bank-approved hedging line and SAFE derivative qualification under the real-demand principle.

FX options, both purchased and written, conducted with the settlement bank under the SAFE-approved derivatives framework, including zero-cost collars, subject to the bank's suitability and realisation test.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps solely for long-term FDI debt or registered equity situations, requiring prior SAFE capital-account approval.

Explicitly excluded: offshore CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for onshore entities. The joint venture's TWD exposure is hedged indirectly through onshore USD FX forwards and natural revenue matching in USD, because TWD is not a freely tradable currency onshore.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and corporate officer/10%+ shareholder information confirmation under Article 22-1 of the Company Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Commercial Registration / One-Stop Company Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March each year covering the preceding fiscal year; intervening changes to directors, supervisors, managers, or shareholders holding 10% or more are filed within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine on the responsible person of NT$1,000–NT$50,000 per infraction; continuing non-compliance may trigger MOEA inspection and, in aggravated cases, administrative dissolution or revocation of registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Adoption of annual financial statements at the Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting and filing of the approved statements with the competent authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Commercial Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary meeting for a calendar-year company must be held by 30 June; approved financial statements and related resolutions must be filed with MOEA within 15 days after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-adoption or non-filing exposes responsible persons to fines under the Company Act and remedial orders; prolonged default can lead to MOEA administrative strike-off or dissolution action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and unappropriated earnings surtax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance – National Taxation Administration (NTB) regional office with jurisdiction over the JV
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May through 31 May of the year following the assessment year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharges, interest, and penalties for underpayment up to three times the evaded tax; continued default results in official assessment and compulsory execution against the JV's assets and may support MOEA dissolution if the company becomes inoperative

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Recurring Business Tax (VAT) return and payment (monthly or quarterly)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration (NTB) – local Revenue Service Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly filers file by the 15th day of the following month; quarterly filers file by the 15th day of the month following the quarter end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of up to NT$100,000, overdue tax surcharge of 1% per two-day period up to 15%, and late payment interest; persistent non-compliance may lead to compulsory collection and suspension of the business registration in serious cases

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Taiwan requires CPA-certified annual financial statements for companies (a) with paid-in capital of NT$30 million or more, (b) designated by the competent authority under Article 20 of the Company Act, or (c) required by the tax authority to provide certified statements. The CN/TW JV shall obtain an independent audit if it meets any threshold or if the Chinese parent's financing agreements require audited statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public and FSC-regulated companies use IFRS as adopted in Taiwan; non-public companies apply the Commercial Accounting Act and Taiwan GAAP (Business Entity Accounting Standards), and may additionally produce IFRS-compliant statements when the JV agreement or foreign parent requires consolidation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On or before 31 March annually, the JV must confirm on the MOEA portal the current list of directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders owning 10% or more of the registered capital as of 31 December; share transfer effects must be registered promptly, and a change occurring during the year is likewise filed within 15 days. The annual confirmation is separate from tax filing and operates as an ongoing transparency audit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Meetings
